'''Alexey Viktorovich Shved''' ([[Russian language|Russian]]: Алексей Викторович Швед; born December 16, 1988) is a Russian professional [[basketball]] player for [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]]. Standing at {{height|m=1.98}}, he plays at both the [[shooting guard]] and [[point guard]] positions. After helping lead CSKA Moscow to the [[2012 Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague final]] in [[2011–12 Euroleague|2012]], Shved spent three years in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], before returning to Europe and earning an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in [[2017–18 Euroleague|2018]]. As a member of the [[Russia national basketball team|Russian national team]], he won the bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], as well as a bronze medal at [[EuroBasket 2011]]. ==Professional career== ===CSKA Moscow (2006–2012)=== Shved began his professional career with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in a [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Super League]] game, against [[PBC Ural Great Perm|Ural Great Perm]], on November 4, 2006.{{Cite web|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/gm/?a=boxscore&id=365&lang=en|title=CSKABasket.com Russian Superleague (Division A): Regular season 04.11.2006, Moscow, 2500 spectators.|access-date=June 5, 2012|archive-date=September 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923211547/http://www.cskabasket.com/gm/?a=boxscore&id=365&lang=en|url-status=dead}} He made his [[EuroLeague]] debut in a game against [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]], on January 17, 2007.{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?pcode=KVZ&gamecode=143&seasoncode=E2006|title=CSKA Moscow vs. Zalgiris - Game|website=www.euroleague.net}} In February 2007, he joined [[BC Khimki|Khimki Moscow Region]], [[Loan (sports)|on loan]] from CSKA Moscow. He then returned to CSKA Moscow before the start of the 2007–08 season. In December 2009, he moved to [[MBC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]], on loan from CSKA Moscow. He moved back to CSKA Moscow before the start of the 2010–11 season. The following season, he reached the [[2012 Euroleague Final Four#Final|EuroLeague Final]] with the Reds.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2012–2014)=== On July 23, 2012, CSKA Moscow announced the departure of Shved in order to sign with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the NBA.{{cite web | url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=11384&lang=en | title=Alexey Shved moves to Minnesota | work=CSKABasket.com | date=July 23, 2012 | access-date=July 23, 2012 | archive-date=October 1, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001223956/http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=11384&lang=en | url-status=dead }} Two days later, he signed a multi-year deal with the Timberwolves.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-free-agent-alexey-shved | title=Wolves Sign Free Agent Alexey Shved | work=NBA.com | date = July 25, 2012 | access-date = July 25, 2012}} === Philadelphia 76ers (2014) === On August 23, 2014, a three-team trade was completed, involving the Timberwolves, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. As part of the deal, Shved and teammate [[Luc Mbah a Moute]] were traded to the Sixers, along with a 2015 first round draft pick from Cleveland. The Cavaliers received [[Kevin Love]] from Minnesota, whereas the Wolves received [[Andrew Wiggins]] and [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]] from Cleveland and [[Thaddeus Young]] from Philadelphia.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140823-trade-details|title=Philadelphia 76ers Acquire 2015 First-round Pick From Minnesota|date=August 23, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=August 23, 2014}} === Houston Rockets (2014–2015) === On December 19, 2014, Shved was acquired by the [[Houston Rockets]] in a three-team trade that also involved the 76ers and the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-veterans-corey-brewer-and-alexey-shved-three-team-trade-timberwolves-and-76ers|title=Rockets Acquire Veterans Corey Brewer and Alexey Shved in Three-Team Trade with Timberwolves and 76ers | Houston Rockets}} === New York Knicks (2015) === On February 19, 2015, Shved was traded, along with two second-round picks, to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Pablo Prigioni]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire-alexey-shved-and-two-draft-picks|title=Knicks Acquire Alexey Shved and Two Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}} ===Khimki (2015–2021)=== On July 16, 2015, Shved returned to Russia, and signed a three-year contract with [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].{{cite news|title=Khimki lands high-flying guard Shved|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/67ff8ni7sb9epwp3|access-date=July 16, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 16, 2015}} The contract was worth $10.2 million net income over three years.{{Cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/alexey-shved-becomes-highest-paid-player-outside-of-us-071615|title=Alexey Shved becomes highest-paid player outside of US.}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/alexey-shved-nba-contract-highest-paid-basketball-player/1tui3mvd14pnh1tuwxxzatph6a|title=Alexey Shved turns down Knicks to become highest-paid player overseas|website=www.sportingnews.com}} On March 27, 2017, Shved was named the [[European professional club basketball system|European-wide second tier level]] [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]'s [[EuroCup Basketball MVP|season MVP]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/item/7pbo3fff78guj7nq|title=7DAYS EuroCup MVP for 2016-17: Alexey Shved, Khimki Moscow Region|website=Welcome to 7DAYS EuroCup}}{{dead link|date=February 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} He was the first player in EuroCup history to average at least 22 points, 5 assists, and 4 rebounds per game in the same season. Shved was awarded the [[VTB United League MVP]] award for the 2016–17 season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/vtb/456959/alexey-shved-named-season-mvp-vtb-league/|title=Alexey Shved named season MVP in VTB League|date=May 30, 2017|website=Eurohoops}} In July 2017, Shved extended his contract with Khimki, through the 2019–20 season.{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/item/7yptlfr9aihadyjw|title=Khimki extends EuroCup MVP Shved|website=Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL}} In 2017–18 season, Khimki made it to the [[2018 EuroLeague Playoffs]] quarterfinals, where they were eliminated by CSKA Moscow, with 3–1 series result. Over the season, Shved led the EuroLeague in scoring, with a career-high 21.8 points per game, which earned him the [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]].{{cite news|title=EuroLeague Alphonso Ford Top Scorer: Alexey Shved, Khimki|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8pww997bgoa63bjs/euroleague-alphonso-ford-top-scorer-alexey-shved-khimki|access-date=May 7, 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=May 7, 2018}} In May 2018, he was named the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] for the [[2017–18 EuroLeague|2017–18 season]].{{cite news|title=2017-18 All-EuroLeague Second Team presented by 7DAYS|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8qbb3a9iw6ykxips/2017-18-all-euroleague-second-team-presented-by-7days|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=May 10, 2018}} ===Return to CSKA Moscow (2021–2023)=== On August 12, 2021, Shved officially returned to CSKA Moscow of the [[VTB United League]], and of the [[EuroLeague]] until it was suspended due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Кому бы он пригодился в России? |url=https://www.sport-express.net/basketball/vtb-league/reviews/aleksey-shved-mozhet-vernutsya-v-edinuyu-ligu-vtb-otchislenie-iz-shansi-i-varianty-v-rossii-2284585/ |website=Спорт-Экспресс |access-date=December 30, 2024 |date=December 24, 2024}} === Zenit Saint Petersburg (2025)=== On January 18, 2025, Shved signed with [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]].{{cite web |title=Alexey Shved is at Zenit! |url=https://bc-zenit.com/en/news/10058|access-date=January 18, 2025 |date=January 18, 2025}} === UNICS Kazan (2025–present)=== On November 4, 2025, Shved signed with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]].{{cite web |title=Алексей Швед – в УНИКСе!|url=https://unics.ru/news/novosti-komandy/?id=aleksey-shved--v-unikse|language=ru|access-date=November 5, 2025|date=November 4, 2025}} ==National team career== [[File:Lithuania vs. Russia in quarter finals of Men's Basketball..jpg|Alexey Shved (right) in a game between [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]] and [[Russia national basketball team|Russia]]|thumb|right]] Shved played with the Russian junior national teams. He played at the [[2006 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], and at the [[2007 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2007]] and [[2008 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2008]] [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]s. Shved has also been a member of the senior men's [[Russia national basketball team|Russian national basketball team]]. He won the bronze medal at the [[EuroBasket 2011]]. At the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], on August 12, 2012, Shved scored 25 points, to lead the Russian national team to an 81–77 victory, over [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]], in the bronze medal game.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}} He also played with Russia at the [[EuroBasket 2013]], and at the [[EuroBasket 2017]],{{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/lid_38135_cp/1/pid/47740/q/shved/rpp//_//players.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014105656/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/lid_38135_cp/1/pid/47740/q/Shved/rpp/_/players.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October
